fact: Ecofin Agency reports the Trans-Saharan Fiber Optic Backbone (DTS), a key part of Chad's regional interconnection strategy with planned links to Niger, Nigeria, Algeria, Libya and Egypt, is 60% complete.
system: Trans-Saharan Fiber Optic Backbone (Dorsale Transsaharienne, DTS)
source_slug: 2026-02-13 Chad Plans 50 Telecom Sites, 50 km of Fiber in N'Djamena

fact: Tchadinfos reports a ministry delegation inspected construction of the technical sites and fibre installation of the Trans-Saharan Backbone (DTS), which links Chad to the Mediterranean network via Niger; works launched in 2023 are slowed, and vandalism was found at the Bol site.
Tchadinfos reports the DTS project has European Union financing of 29 million euros, and that its works began in 2023.

We Are Tech Africa reports the Chadian component of the Trans-Saharan Fiber Optic Backbone, launched in May 2023 with the CGPS/LORYNE consortium, was 32% complete at the minister's 6 March 2025 visit and well behind its ten-month schedule; it is expected to enable interconnection with Niger, Mali, Nigeria, Mauritania and Algeria.

Connecting Africa reports the N'Djamena-Mbere fibre route to the Cameroon border is not yet started: the April 2025 Sotel-Airtel MoU was suspended by ARCEP over sovereignty clauses and must be revised before work can begin, and the government urged the operators on 9 February 2026 to restart talks.

The African Development Bank committed US$33.9 million in 2019 for the Chad component of the Trans-Saharan fibre backbone, installing 1,510 km of optical fibre across Niger and Chad, with one section in Chad; the record lists it as active with US$18.2 million disbursed and an end year of 2026, and states no start of works.

The article says the six CEMAC countries, of which it names Chad as a landlocked market, are developing the Central African Backbone to interconnect their national fibre networks, backed by about $273 million from member states and development partners; it gives no date for the agreement or start of works, so the document's published date is used.

A project official said the fibre link from Libya to the Chadian border should be completed by end 2026, with the connection with Chad already engaged with Chadian authorities and telecom firms (Le N'Djam Post).
